title: Simulation-Free Single-Fraction Radiation Therapy for Indolent Lymphoma
summary:
This pilot study will evaluate whether people with indolent B-cell lymphoma can receive radiation therapy without a separate computed tomography (CT) simulation appointment. Participants will receive one low-dose radiation treatment of 4 gray (Gy). Treatment planning will use a recent diagnostic CT scan, and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging on the treatment day will be used to confirm participant positioning and adjust the treatment plan if needed.

The study includes participants with orbital or ocular adnexal lymphoma and participants with lymphoma at other body sites. The investigators will assess whether simulation-free treatment can be completed successfully, treatment duration, the number of hospital visits required, treatment side effects, patient-reported symptoms, control of the treated lymphoma site, and the need for additional treatment. Participants will be followed for up to 12 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Histologically confirmed indolent B-cell lymphoma, including marginal zone/mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma, follicular lymphoma grades 1-2, small lymphocytic lymphoma, or mantle cell lymphoma.
* Disease requiring focal radiation therapy with 4 Gy delivered in one fraction for local control or symptom relief.
* Lesion anatomy suitable for single-fraction radiation therapy and simulation-free, CBCT-guided treatment delivery, as determined by the treating radiation oncologist.
* Available diagnostic CT imaging suitable for contouring and dose calculation that encompasses the full intended target and relevant organs at risk:
* Obtained within 2 months before treatment for orbital or ocular adnexal disease.
* Obtained within 6 weeks before treatment for non-orbital disease.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-3, with the ability to tolerate treatment positioning and delivery.
* Localized or advanced-stage disease is permitted, provided the target lesion is appropriate for focal treatment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnostic imaging that does not meet the minimum quality requirements for treatment planning or falls outside the required time window.
* Disease anatomy unsuitable for simulation-free delivery, such as inability to maintain stable positioning, excessive motion, or inadequate CBCT visualization.
* Prior radiation therapy to the same site if re-irradiation using the study workflow is considered clinically inappropriate.
* Bulky disease greater than 6 centimeters for which single-fraction 4 Gy radiation therapy is unlikely to provide adequate local control, as determined by the treating physician.
* Requirement for urgent systemic therapy because of widespread or symptomatic disease.
